vfr.label: Variable frame rate
vfr.why: Frames are not evenly spaced in time. Editors expect a constant rate; uneven timing makes the timeline drift, audio slip out of sync, or the editor crash on import.

fps_mismatch.label: Frame rate
fps_mismatch.why: The clip runs at a different rate than your project. Mixing rates on one timeline forces the editor to drop or repeat frames on the fly, which looks choppy and costs playback speed.

hdr.label: HDR
hdr.why: HDR footage on a normal Rec.709 timeline looks washed out or clipped unless it is tone-mapped first.

hevc_10bit.label: 10-bit HEVC
hevc_10bit.why: 10-bit HEVC is very heavy to decode and not supported everywhere; scrubbing stutters or the clip refuses to play.

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.why: Clips above the project size waste disk and processing power, and odd frame sizes make some codecs fail.

audio_rate.label: Audio rate
audio_rate.why: Video projects run at 48 kHz. Other rates get resampled during playback, which can drift over long clips.

rotation.label: Rotation in metadata
rotation.why: Phones store rotation as a flag. Some editors ignore it and show the clip sideways.

no_audio.label: No audio
no_audio.why: Without an audio track the clip behaves differently from the rest when you link or sync sound.

insv.label: Insta360 original
insv.why: 360° originals need reframing in Insta360 Studio before any editor can use them.

corrupt.label: Damaged file
corrupt.why: The file cannot be read reliably. Re-encoding would hide the damage, so Clipcura leaves it for you to check.

color_space.label: Colours
color_space.why: The pixels are coded in BT.601. On a Rec.709 timeline colours shift slightly unless they are converted.

loudness.label: Loudness
loudness.why: Clips cut together at different loudness jump in volume, and peaks above the ceiling distort on phones. Only reported unless the profile turns on the fix, because normalising changes the sound.

start.name: Start
start.purpose: Check a folder of footage. Clipcura reads every clip and tells you what would trip up the edit. Nothing is changed at this point.
steps: Pick the profile on the right. It sets the target frame rate, the largest size and the codec of the converted files.
Drop a folder on the viewfinder, use Choose folder, or paste the path and press Scan.
If Clipcura may not read the folder yet, confirm Allow and scan. It only reads and writes inside allowed folders.
When the scan finishes, the scan result opens.
tips: Originals are never changed. Converted files go to a separate folder, by default 02_edit next to your footage folder.
Recent folders can be scanned again with one click.
The panel on the right shows what this computer converts with: GPU, video memory, free space and the measured fastest paths.

results.name: Scan result
results.purpose: Every clip of the scanned folder with what Clipcura found, and the conversion of the clips that need it.
steps: The cards at the top count the clips: ready, fixable, needing a person, errors. Click a card to show only those clips.
Fixable clips are selected for you. Change the selection and press Fix.
Check the summary: what will be written, where, and how much space it needs. Then start the conversion.
Open a clip to see the measured values, why each finding matters for the edit, the same frame before and after, and the exact ffmpeg command.
tips: Needing a person means Clipcura cannot fix it safely, for example 360° originals that have to be exported from Insta360 Studio first.
Clips converted before are skipped, so scanning and fixing the same folder again is safe.

jobs.name: Jobs
jobs.purpose: Conversions in progress and finished ones, with speed and time left.
steps: A running job shows its progress, processing speed and time left. A waiting job starts as soon as a slot is free.
Cancel a job with its button. The half-written file is deleted; the original stays untouched.
A finished job shows where the converted file is.
tips: Jobs marked AI were requested by an assistant and approved by you.
Closing the window keeps Clipcura running in the notification area. Its icon fills up as the batch progresses, and Windows tells you when the batch is done.
How many jobs run at once on the GPU and the CPU is set in Settings.

activity.name: AI activity
activity.purpose: What assistants and automations did through Clipcura, and the requests waiting for your approval.
steps: A request from an assistant appears at the top with a summary of what would happen.
Approve or reject each request, or all of them at once. Nothing is converted before you approve.
The timeline below records every action: who did it, when and with what result.
tips: Assistants may scan and prepare plans on their own. Converting waits for you while approval is on in Settings.
Assistants cannot add allowed folders or approve their own requests.

settings.name: Settings
settings.purpose: How Clipcura works on this computer: the folders it may use, assistants, jobs at once, profiles and appearance.
steps: Allowed folders: add the folders with your footage. Clipcura reads and writes only inside them.
Assistants and jobs: keep approval on so assistants ask before converting, and set how many jobs run at once.
Profiles: edit a built-in profile or duplicate it to make your own. An edited built-in profile can be reset to the default.
Updates: a daily check for new versions (only if you turn it on), and buttons to download a new version or a missing part.
Appearance: theme, accent colour, language and animations, and whether Clipcura opens in its own window or in your default browser.
tips: System shows what clipcura doctor measured on this computer. Run it again after a graphics driver update.

about.name: About
about.purpose: Who makes Clipcura, under which licence, and the software it is built from.
steps: Licence texts shows the full licence of every component. They travel with the program, as their licences require.
tips: FFmpeg does the actual conversion. It runs as a separate program under its own GPL licence; the link leads to its source code.

log.name: Log
log.purpose: Where to look when something goes wrong: what each part of Clipcura did, newest first, updated live.
steps: Choose what to show: errors only, warnings and errors, or everything.
Search for a file name, a job or a word from an error message.
Technical details under an entry show the full error for a bug report.
Copy shown entries puts them on the clipboard, e.g. for an issue on GitHub.
tips: The access key is never written to the log, so the entries can be shared.
An assistant connected over MCP reads the same entries with get_logs.
